14K likes, 748 comments - luke_coutinho on February 18, 2026: "For years, healthcare has been treated like isolated compartments. One system for symptoms. Another for side effects. Another for “lifestyle.” And somewhere in between, the human system gets neglected.

I’ve sat with people on medication, people undergoing chemotherapy, people choosing Ayurveda, homeopathy, or natural therapies. Different paths. Different choices. All valid when done responsibly and scientifically. But what often gets missed is this: every path depends on the strength of the body walking it.

You don’t build a house by focusing only on the roof. You start with the base. Yet many of us are trying to heal with foundations that are exhausted, inflamed, undernourished, sleep-deprived, emotionally overloaded, and biologically out of rhythm.

This is why we announce Foundational Medicine.

It is not an alternative to modern medicine.
It is not a replacement for treatment.
It is the support system that allows treatment to work better.

When sleep is regulated, inflammation is reduced, nutrients are restored, stress is managed, the gut is supported, emotions are processed, and daily rhythms are respected, the body becomes more resilient. More receptive. More capable of recovery.

Foundational Medicine asks one grounding question before everything else:
Is the body stable enough to heal well?

At Team Luke, this is not just a concept; it is how we work. Our approach is backed by a distinguished Advisory Board of leading clinicians across specialties, ensuring medical depth, ethical rigour, and scientific alignment. Every expert across nutrition, lifestyle medicine, emotional health, movement, breathwork, and clinical support is trained under a shared framework with accountability, continuous learning, and a commitment to personalised, foundation-led care.

Because long-term health is not built on quick fixes. It is built when foundations are understood, strengthened, and honoured — quietly, consistently, and with compassion.

#FoundationalMedicine #IntegrativeMedicine #LifestyleMedicine #RootCauseHealing #HolisticHealth PreventiveHealth MindBodyConnection HealthFoundations".

Their lungs will never fully grow.
Adults are developing chronic breathlessness and inflammation.

20K likes, 682 comments - luke_coutinho on January 7, 2026: "Imagine not being able to swallow food for months. Losing weight, strength & hope. Feeling helpless, exhausted & unsure whether the treatment itself will break you before the disease does.

And now imagine reaching a place of complete disease regression. ✅ 

This is Atul’s story.

At 60, Atul lived an ordinary life, daily walks, swimming & family time. A routine health check changed everything. What began as low Hb levels & acidity quietly unfolded into stomach cancer. Chemo, partial gastrectomy & severe side effects followed.

Then came the hardest phase…an esophageal stricture that made swallowing nearly impossible. For months, he was on liquids, watching his body weaken & his spirit collapse.

When Atul came to us, he had already endured chemo, surgery, recurrence fear, extreme weight loss, nutritional depletion & emotional exhaustion.

Our intention was never to replace medical treatment, but to rebuild the foundation so his body could receive the remaining treatment better. ☝️ 

Our work focused on:

👍Reducing inflammation & cancer-supportive pathways
✔️ Anti-angiogenic nutrition, DNA repair, stem cell regeneration, immune strengthening
❗️Nutrition adapted to swallowing limitations
🦠Rebuilding gut health & microbiome
💪🏻 Muscle mass & strength routines
🙌🏻Emotional healing through breathwork, visualization, journaling, gratitude
✨Lymphatic & circadian rhythm support
🙏🏻Restoring hope, faith & purpose

Throughout this journey, his family stood by him, not just as support, but medicine.

Slowly, his body responded. Swallowing improved. Energy returned. Fear softened. Weight stabilized. Even during treatment, he traveled, walked 10k steps, trained with weights & stayed consistent with his routine.

Today, Atul is in complete disease regression. 

In his words,

“I stopped looking like a patient & started living again.”

Treatment alone is not enough. Chemo, surgery & radiation treat cancer, but healing cannot happen on a broken foundation. Medical care is doctor’s role. Building foundation through nutrition, lifestyle, sleep, mindset, emotional health & consistency is ours.

Take your treatment. But build your foundation

We help you find the way. 🤝".

803 likes, 31 comments - luke_coutinho on October 10, 2026: "Sometimes, without realising it, the things we say to our ageing parents can make them feel that getting older means slowly giving up on life.

“Don't lift anything heavy.”
“You're getting old, forgetting is normal.”
“At this age, why change anything?”
“You've worked enough. Just rest now.”

Most of these things come from a place of love, concern and wanting to protect them.

But are we sometimes confusing protection with limitation?

One thing I've learnt through years of working with people across different age groups is that ageing doesn't mean we stop needing strength, movement, purpose, connection or independence.

In fact, these things become even more important as we grow older.

Our parents still need to build and maintain muscle. They need nourishing food, quality sleep, mental stimulation, meaningful relationships and something to look forward to every morning.

They need to feel heard, valued and capable.

And when they experience pain, memory changes, fatigue or emotional struggles, we shouldn't automatically dismiss everything as "just old age."

Of course, ageing brings physiological changes. Some people may have medical conditions, mobility limitations or health complications that require individualised care and professional guidance.

But that doesn't mean we stop working on the foundations of good health.

This is what we believe in Foundational Medicine.

It's never too late to improve a habit, learn something new, build strength or find a new purpose.

And perhaps, as children, one of the greatest gifts we can give our parents is not just taking care of them, but encouraging them to continue taking care of themselves.

To remind them that their life still has so much to offer.

You cannot stop ageing. But you can influence how you age.

❤️ Share this with someone who has ageing parents. Sometimes, changing the way we speak to them can change the way they see their own ageing.

#HealthyAgeing #FoundationalMedicine #SeniorHealth #LifestyleMedicine #AgeingWell".

1,256 likes, 27 comments - luke_coutinho on October 10, 2026: "We have so much health information available today. Research papers, podcasts, fitness trackers, health apps, supplements, and a new wellness trend almost every week.

And somewhere in all this information, we've started overcomplicating something that often begins with common sense.

We're looking for the next breakthrough, the next supplement, the next biohack, while sometimes overlooking the simplest things our bodies need.

We know that sleeping four hours every night isn't healthy. Yet we compromise on sleep.

We know our bodies need movement. Yet we spend most of our day sitting.

We know real food nourishes us. Yet convenience often takes priority.

And we know that relationships, laughter, fresh air, sunlight, and emotional well-being matter. Yet they're often the first things we neglect.

Now, don't get me wrong.

Science is important. Research is important. Medical investigations, treatments, and professional guidance are absolutely necessary, especially when we're dealing with health complications, chronic conditions, or symptoms that need attention.

This is not suggesting that common sense can replace medical science.

But when it comes to maintaining our everyday health, do we really need to make everything so complicated?

This is something we keep coming back to in Foundational Medicine.

Before looking for something extraordinary, have we taken care of the ordinary?

Our sleep. Our food. Our movement. Our relationships. Our emotional health. Our daily habits.

Sometimes, better health isn't about adding another thing to your routine. It's about consistently doing the things you already know matter.

Be educated, not influenced.

Share this with someone who needs a reminder that taking care of their health doesn't always have to be complicated. 🌿

#FoundationalMedicine #HealthyLiving #LifestyleMedicine #HealthAwareness #Wellness".

505 likes, 26 comments - luke_coutinho on October 9, 2026: "Sometimes the shoulder is where the story shows up… but not necessarily where the story begins.

Frozen shoulder, or adhesive capsulitis, involves pain and progressive restriction of shoulder movement. But certain whole-body factors may influence susceptibility and recovery.

A few things worth understanding:

🔹 Insulin resistance matters: Persistently elevated blood glucose can affect collagen and connective tissue through processes such as glycation, potentially contributing to stiffness.

🔹 Thyroid health is worth checking: Both underactive and overactive thyroid conditions have been associated with frozen shoulder. That doesn’t mean thyroid dysfunction is the cause in every case, but it can be one piece of the puzzle.

🔹 Menopause is more than estrogen: During this transition, changes in muscle mass, sleep, body composition, recovery and pain sensitivity can all influence musculoskeletal health.

🔹 Movement matters: Completely avoiding movement because of pain can worsen stiffness. Appropriate, gradual mobility under the guidance of a physiotherapist can support recovery.

🔹 Muscle is metabolic health: Resistance training in midlife supports strength, glucose regulation, bone health and physical function not just muscle size.

One important point: frozen shoulder can happen even when blood sugar, thyroid and hormones are normal.

And persistent shoulder pain isn't always frozen shoulder. Rotator cuff problems, arthritis and even neck-related pain can cause similar symptoms, which is why proper assessment matters.

Don’t try to find one single cause from one blood test.

Look at the bigger picture while treating the shoulder itself.

Sleep. Movement. Nutrition. Muscle. Stress management. Metabolic health. Emotional wellbeing.

This is the lens of Foundational Medicine: not replacing treatment, but strengthening the foundations that support the body alongside appropriate medical and physiotherapy care.

Your shoulder may need attention.

But sometimes, it can also remind you to pay attention to the rest of your health.

#FrozenShoulder #MenopauseHealth #WomensHealth #MetabolicHealth #HealthyAging".

548 likes, 92 comments - luke_coutinho on October 9, 2026: "78 participants. One classroom. Different journeys. One shared vision.

What began as an idea to bring Foundational Medicine into a classroom became something truly meaningful on September 26, 2026.

India’s first batch of the Foundational Medicine & Lifestyle Certification - Level 1: Find Your Rhythm with Luke Coutinho came together at the Harvard Business Classroom, Taj Lands End, Mumbai.

And what a day it was.

A room filled with curiosity, questions, conversations, diverse perspectives and a willingness to look at health differently.

We came together with one purpose: to move beyond isolated information and understand how the foundations of human health connect.

Nutrition. Movement. Sleep. Emotional wellness. Recovery. Our environment. The interconnected systems that shape our health every day.

Through discussions, real-world cases, reflection and shared learning, we explored what it means to look beyond symptoms, connect the dots and understand the body as a whole.

Because education isn't simply about knowing more. It's about expanding how we think, question and apply what we learn.

One of the most meaningful moments was watching conversations turn into insights, strangers become a community, and months of preparation come together in one shared experience.

And as our first cohort received their certificates, we celebrated something beyond a milestone.

We celebrated the commitment to keep learning, growing and carrying this understanding into everyday life.

To our first 78 participants, thank you for being part of this beginning. Your curiosity, energy and participation made this experience what it was.

What began in one classroom now carries forward through many different journeys.

This was our first chapter. And we're looking forward to everything that comes next.

#FoundationalMedicine #LifestyleMedicine #LukeCoutinho #FindYourRhythm #HealthEducation".

5,671 likes, 162 comments - luke_coutinho on October 8, 2026: "We talk about the pressure of arranged marriages. But do we talk enough about what that pressure can do to our health?

At 29, she was happy with her life. A career she loved, friends, independence, and the excitement of finding a partner.

Then came the meetings. The comparisons. The rejections. The unsolicited opinions.

“Can she lose weight?”
“She's too career-focused.”
“She's already 29?”

No single comment broke her confidence. But slowly, they started adding up.

And her body began responding too.

Poor sleep. Bloating. Acne. Irregular periods. Exhaustion.

When she came to us, we looked beyond her symptoms. We explored when they began, what had changed in her life, and the emotional stress she had been carrying.

Because chronic psychological stress can influence our nervous system, gut-brain axis, sleep, hormonal regulation, and inflammatory pathways.

Through the lens of Foundational Medicine, we worked on restoring her foundations. Sleep. Nourishment. Movement. Strength training. Emotional wellbeing. And helping her family understand the difference between support and pressure.

Gradually, her sleep improved. Her gut settled. Her skin cleared. Her cycles became more regular.

But the biggest shift wasn't physical.

She stopped seeing rejection as proof that something was wrong with her.

Sometimes, healing also means changing the conversations we have with ourselves.

And if you're navigating the marriage process, remember:

You're not just waiting to be chosen. You're choosing too.

Share this with someone who needs this reminder.

{mental health, arranged marriage, emotional wellbeing, chronic stress, gut brain axis, hormonal health, women's health, foundational medicine, self worth, lifestyle medicine, holistic health, mind body connection, stress management, healing, India}".

6,086 likes, 6,069 comments - luke_coutinho on October 8, 2026: "One of the biggest misconceptions about fasting is that eating less automatically means you're doing something good for your body.

But that's not always the case.

Over the years, I've seen how easily fasting can turn into a routine of long gaps between meals, very little protein, and then one heavy meal at the end of the day.

And sometimes, we don't even realise it.

We feel tired, experience cravings, struggle with digestion, or find ourselves reaching for something sweet just to get through the day.

Now, fasting has a beautiful place in our traditions. It's a time for devotion, discipline, reflection, and connecting with something deeper.

And I believe we can respect that while also respecting our body's physiology.

Here's something worth understanding.

Fasting and nourishment are not opposites.

You don't necessarily have to eat large quantities to nourish yourself well. What matters is how you put your meals together, the quality of your ingredients, and whether you're giving your body what it needs.

For example, instead of making your fasting meals entirely carbohydrate-based, you can explore combinations that offer a better balance of nutrients.

You can also experiment with different ways of preparing familiar fasting ingredients. A few thoughtful additions or swaps can make your meals more satisfying without making your time in the kitchen complicated.

And remember, there's no single way to fast.

Some people follow one meal a day. Others eat several smaller meals using permitted ingredients. Some avoid particular foods, while others follow different family traditions.

Your nutritional needs will also depend on your age, activity levels, health conditions, and the type of fast you're observing.

The goal is not to make fasting another stressful diet or a competition in restriction.

It's to find a rhythm that honours your beliefs and supports your well-being.

362 likes, 76 comments - luke_coutinho on October 7, 2026: "Dr Rohini came to us at her lowest.

A doctor who spent years helping others feel better had quietly placed her own health last.

Not because she didn’t care. She simply knew how to care for everyone else first.

Since childhood, she had taken responsibility for her family. She continued running her dental practice, raising her daughter & caring for everyone.

Years of stress, loss & anxiety showed up as acidity, constipation, headaches, disturbed sleep, weight gain & food fear.

Despite counselling, medication 💊 & 500 hours of yoga 🧘‍♂️ training, she didn’t feel like herself.

She reached out seeking help with burnout.

We asked for her latest blood work.

She paused. She couldn’t remember her last preventive screening.

Investigations revealed a shocking discovery: a large fibroid.

Suddenly, everything changed.

She was heading into surgery with low Hb, poor gut health & significant anxiety.

So we didn’t begin with weight management.

We began with foundations for surgery & recovery.

With digestion severely disturbed, we designed a personalised liquid nutrition plan supporting hydration, digestion & nutritional needs.

Surgery followed, along with jaundice, typhoid, psoriasis & hydrosalpinx.

Her protocol evolved with every stage of recovery.

We focused on:

• Gut, immune & nutritional support
• Sleep, circadian rhythm & hydration
• Gentle movement & walking
• Nervous-system regulation & breathwork
• Emotional health & boundaries
• Creativity, hobbies & joy

Slowly, things changed.

Her gut stabilised. Acidity settled. Sleep improved. Haemoglobin rose. She maintained muscle despite bed rest, without gaining weight.

But her biggest recovery wasn’t on a report.

It was in her relationship with herself.

She rediscovered painting, cooking, writing & music. Today, she sings her heart out at karaoke! 🎤 

She is preparing to return to dentistry, inspired to explore preventive health.

This is foundational medicine. Understanding the whole person, adapting to their needs & rebuilding health from the ground up.

To every healthcare professional silently experiencing burnout:

You need care too.

We help you find a way 🤝".
